question: A 50-year-old asymptomatic woman comes for a routine check-up. Which of the following screening tests is MOST appropriate to offer her TODAY to detect early cervical cancer?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CA-125 is a tumour marker for ovarian cancer monitoring; it is NOT recommended as a population-level cervical cancer screening tool.
Correct. Pap smear (or HPV co-test) is the recommended secondary prevention tool for cervical cancer. Women aged 21–65 years should be screened; cytology every 3 years or HPV co-test every 5 years.
Transvaginal ultrasound is not validated as a cervical cancer screening tool; it is used in ovarian and endometrial cancer evaluation.
Colposcopy is a diagnostic procedure for abnormal Pap smear results, not a primary screening test for asymptomatic women.

overallFeedback.feedback: Pap smear (cervical cytology) is the evidence-based screening tool for cervical cancer. CA-125 and TVS have no role in cervical cancer screening.
Correct. Pap smear is the standard secondary prevention screening tool for cervical cancer — it detects pre-invasive lesions (CIN 1-3) before they progress.
